methods: Verify every source-file SHA-256 against the pinned import commit before patching.
Apply each proof only in an isolated temporary copy; do not modify the imported source branch.

Compile every exact changed module when its pinned dependency cache is available; otherwise compile the exact changed declaration/body against the same Lean and mathlib revisions through an explicitly recorded narrowed-import or dependency-interface harness.
Import the fresh module or declaration-harness oleans and run #print axioms for every audited declaration.
Reject a candidate if any changed declaration's exact axioms list contains sorryAx.
For proof-replacement candidates, require every candidate-scoped sorry to be replaced in the patched temporary source file and require the before/replaced/after counts to reconcile.
Require zero residual direct sorry for a complete candidate; preserve and report residual direct sorry for a partial candidate.
Treat direct-sorry coverage and textbook semantic coverage as independent: a candidate may close every current sorry while an unformalized part of the source statement remains recorded.

For a tracked repair, preserve a replayable patch, verify its SHA-256, replay it with `git apply --unidiff-zero` against the pinned source, and verify the resulting source hashes and direct-sorry counts before checking compilation evidence.
For a statement or signature candidate, require every audited changed declaration to compile and pass its axioms check without changing a direct sorry count.

declarations.proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact h.exists_regular_value
  · intro h
    exact ⟨h⟩

declarations.proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨h.contMDiff, h.isRegularSublevelSet⟩
  · rintro ⟨hf, hD⟩
    exact ⟨hf, hD⟩

declarations.name: IsBoundaryDefiningFunctionAt.eq_zero
declarations.proof:
by
  obtain ⟨s, _, hp, hzero, _⟩ := hf.2.2
  exact (hzero p hp).mp hf.1

limitations: These proofs were validated in an isolated temporary copy; the pinned imported Lean source remains unchanged.
A validated candidate is ready to apply on a source-repair branch, but its task remains formal_review: pending until that source change is made and the project generators are rerun.
Ten validated candidates are partial: their patched temporary files retain twenty-eight direct sorry tokens outside the candidate scope.

The full Mathlib umbrella cache was unavailable in this cloud workspace. Candidates whose exact transitive closure could not be rebuilt use the per-candidate narrowed-import or dependency-interface harness recorded in moduleCompilation; those scoped checks are not presented as a clean full-project build.
The Example 2.14 changed declarations compile and pass axioms checks in a narrow-import harness, but its whole narrowed candidate file timed out after sixty seconds without a diagnostic.

Problem 5-5 uses exact pinned signatures for two already-proved Example 4.20 dependencies as interface axioms; those theorem names therefore appear in its axioms list, while sorryAx does not. A clean full-project rebuild remains the final integration check.

The Proposition 4.6 composition and finite-product local-diffeomorphism statements are verified; its ambient extended-chart equivalence remains unproved because it is false for boundary models, and the open-submanifold restriction remains semantically incomplete.

The Theorem 4.26 local-section equation helper is verified, but its main equivalence is false for arbitrary models with corners; the same boundary issue invalidates the current Proposition 4.28 open-map generalization.
The Theorem 4.12 submersion and immersion normal forms are verified without using its remaining constant-rank owner hole; that one direct sorry token remains explicit.

The Theorem 4.15 current Lean statement is fully proved, but coverage from Lee's differential-injectivity definition still needs a boundaryless-target bridge; the more general bridge currently stated in `Definition_4_21_extra_1.is_immersion_iff_forall_injective_mfderiv` is false for arbitrary targets with corners.
The downstream Problem 4-3 module compiles with the Theorem 4.15 candidate but retains its own direct sorry in `constant_rank_boundary_local_coordinate_normal_form`.

The Proposition 5.2 candidate closes both current direct sorry tokens and adds a verified identity-diffeomorphism formulation of the textbook's uniqueness claim; the pinned source still has that semantic-coverage finding until the patch is applied.
The downstream Problem 5.1 module compiles with the Proposition 5.2 candidate but retains pre-existing transitive sorryAx from its recorded Chapter 4 owners.
The multi-file Theorem 5.51 helper repair has a tracked replayable patch; its main theorem still depends on the three remaining owner holes and therefore still reports sorryAx.
The statement-addition candidate validates an explicit coverage repair for Theorem 1.37; the pinned source still has that coverage finding until the theorem is applied.
The reported axioms vary by declaration and harness; no audited changed declaration depends on sorryAx.
